The [2024 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NFL_season "2024 NFL season") was the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys")' 65th in the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) and their fifth and final season under [head coach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Dallas_Cowboys_head_coaches "List of Dallas Cowboys head coaches") [Mike McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_McCarthy "Mike McCarthy"). This was their first season since [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2020 Dallas Cowboys season") without [Dan Quinn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Quinn_\(American_football\) "Dan Quinn \(American football\)") as defensive coordinator, as the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders") hired him to be their head coach. He was replaced in that role by former [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings") head coach [Mike Zimmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Zimmer "Mike Zimmer"), who returned to the Cowboys after eighteen years. The Cowboys failed to improve upon their 12–5 record from the past three seasons following a loss to the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Atlanta_Falcons_season "2024 Atlanta Falcons season") in Week 9, and failed to match it after a loss to the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Philadelphia_Eagles_season "2024 Philadelphia Eagles season") in Week 10. After the Eagles defeated the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Carolina_Panthers_season "2024 Carolina Panthers season") in Week 14, the Cowboys were knocked out of NFC East contention, marking the 20th straight season the division would not have a repeat champion. With the Commanders' 36–33 win over the Eagles in Week 16, the Cowboys were eliminated from playoff contention for the first time since [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2020 Dallas Cowboys season").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Dallas_Cowboys_season#cite_note-s162-1) After their 41–7 loss at Philadelphia in Week 17, the Cowboys suffered a losing season for the first time since that same year, and were also swept by the Eagles for the first time since [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2011 Dallas Cowboys season").
For the first time since 2010, offensive tackle [Tyron Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyron_Smith "Tyron Smith") was not on the roster, as he signed with the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_New_York_Jets_season "2024 New York Jets season") during free agency.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Dallas_Cowboys_season#cite_note-2) On April 29, running back [Ezekiel Elliott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezekiel_Elliott "Ezekiel Elliott") signed a one-year contract to return to the team after a year away.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Dallas_Cowboys_season#cite_note-3)
The Cowboys notably struggled at home, going 2–7 at home. Conversely, they performed moderately well on the road with a 5–3 road record. The 2–7 home record notably came after a year in which the Cowboys went undefeated at home in the regular season at 8–0.
After the season, head coach Mike McCarthy's contract expired. It was announced McCarthy would not return to the Cowboys, as the two sides failed to reach an extension, ending McCarthy's tenure in Dallas.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Dallas_Cowboys_season#cite_note-4) Offensive coordinator Brian Schottenheimer was promoted to head coach on January 24, 2025.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Dallas_Cowboys_season#cite_note-5)

While the Cowboys played the Bengals close for most of the game, a devastating special teams blunder would ultimately cost them the game — after the Cowboys blocked a Bengals punt late in the fourth quarter, [Amani Oruwariye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amani_Oruwariye "Amani Oruwariye") would inadvertently touch the ball past the line of scrimmage, which the Bengals recovered. The play was ruled as a muffed catch, giving Cincinnati a fresh set of downs. Three plays later, Joe Burrow threw the go-ahead touchdown pass to Ja'Marr Chase with 1:09 remaining. The Cowboys failed to respond on their final drive, and dropped to 5–8 on the season. This was the Cowboys' first loss to the Bengals since the [2004 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2004 Dallas Cowboys season"), as well as their first home loss to Cincinnati since 1988.

The Cowboys traveled to Philadelphia seeking to avenge their Week 10 loss. A promising opening drive for the Cowboys ended in disaster when Cooper Rush threw a 69-yard pick six to [C. J. Gardner-Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Gardner-Johnson "C. J. Gardner-Johnson") to give the Eagles a 7–0 lead. The Cowboys responded with a twelve-play, 70-yard drive culminating in a game-tying Jalen Tolbert touchdown reception for what ultimately would be Dallas's only points of the afternoon. After the teams traded punts twice, the Eagles reclaimed a 14–7 lead with a DeVonta Smith touchdown and never looked back. The Cowboys turned the ball over twice before halftime, leading to 10 more Eagles points and a 24–7 deficit. Philadelphia then scored 17 points in the second half to put the game out of reach for Dallas. With the crushing 41–7 loss, the Cowboys dropped to 7–9 on the year, thus sealing their first losing season since [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2020 Dallas Cowboys season"). It was also the first time since [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2011 Dallas Cowboys season") that the Cowboys were swept by the Eagles.
